newsitem.title: USA: U.S. companies have pact to divide satellite slots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. companies have pact to divide satellite slots.

text.p: A group of fifteen companies agreed on how to divide up a portion of the airwaves to provide video, data transmission and high-speed Internet access via satellite, the FCC said.

The agreement between the companies -- which include AT&T Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Loral Space & Communications Ltd, and a unit of General Electric Co -- will allow the the Federal Communications Commission to issue satellite licenses for the "Ka-band" of the spectrum.

"The orbital assignment plan agreed on enables the commission to move forward with licensing and thus ensure that these new satellite communications services reach consumers as rapidly as possible," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt said in a statement.
The satellites would be deployed in "region A" of the orbital arc. As a result of the pact, the companies said they withdrew their FCC petitions against one another.
